name: Nilima Motaparti
current_role: Whole-Time Director (Commercial), Divi's Laboratories (listed on company site as Nilima Prasad Divi)
profile: Daughter of Divi's Laboratories founder Murali Divi and a major shareholder of the Hyderabad-based API maker. Joined officially in 2012 as Chief Controller (Commercial); now Whole-Time Director overseeing material sourcing and procurement, capital projects, corporate finance and investor relations.
interesting_fact: She has built Divi's sourcing strategy around a base of alternative suppliers and long-term procurement contracts to cut supply risk; she holds master's degrees in international business (GITAM) and international finance (University of Glasgow).
deep_cut_fact: She first worked at Divi's as a trainee around 1999 while still a graduate, learning finance under CFO L. Kishore Babu; she has quoted her father's advice that although the company is cash rich, 'we still need to spend and think like a small company.'
notes: Company now lists her as Nilima Prasad Divi. Low public profile; she personally oversees investor relations, so the IR route (cs@divislabs.com) is the most relevant.

name: Shao Xiaofeng
current_role: Long-time Alibaba executive (EVP and chair of the Group Risk Management Committee per FY2025 report); left the Alibaba Partnership list in June 2026, current role unclear
profile: Shao Xiaofeng (often written 邵晓锋) joined Alibaba in 2005 from the Hangzhou police, became executive president of Alipay in 2008 and Alibaba's first chief risk officer in 2012, and later served as director at Alibaba Pictures. His fortune comes mainly from his stake in Ant Group. Alibaba's FY2026 annual report (June 2026) showed him leaving the partnership.
interesting_fact: Before joining Alibaba he was a criminal investigator: head of the first brigade of the Hangzhou Public Security Bureau's criminal investigation unit; Chinese media nicknamed him Alibaba's 'old detective' gatekeeper.
deep_cut_fact: Like all Alibaba partners he has a wuxia nickname (花名): his is 'Guo Jing' (郭靖), the righteous hero of Jin Yong's novels, and staff describe him as '侠骨柔情' (chivalrous yet tender).
notes: Name commonly spelled 邵晓锋 in Chinese press (input has 邵晓峰). Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Exit from Alibaba Partnership reported by IT Home, 21 Jun 2026 (https://www.ithome.com/0/966/730.htm). Any approach would go via Alibaba/Ant corporate PR.

name: Jin Xin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (~40%), Dajin Heavy Industry (SZ: 002487)
profile: Jin Xin founded the predecessor of Dajin Heavy Industry in 2001; it moved from building steel structures into power-boiler steelwork (2004) and wind towers (2007) and listed in Shenzhen in 2010 as China's first A-share wind tower/pile maker. Dajin is now a leading supplier of offshore wind monopiles to Europe and is expanding into heavy-lift shipping, marshalling ports and wind-farm development.
interesting_fact: Dajin was reported as the No.1 supplier of European offshore wind monopiles by sales, with share rising from 18.5% in 2024 to 29.1% in H1 2025, and the only Asia-Pacific supplier to deliver monopiles to Europe in batches.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 2001 at age 34 with three production lines he bought himself (H-beam, shot-blasting and colour-plate lines worth RMB 4.8m), backed by his former employer Panpan Group, which supplied RMB 8m of panels and exited a year later.
notes: Highly relevant for an energy podcast (offshore wind supply chain). Jin is non-executive chairman and keeps a low media profile; board secretary/VP Ge Xin handles investor communications. Company filed for a Hong Kong listing in Sept 2025.

name: Shintaro Yamada
current_role: Director, Representative Executive Officer and CEO, Mercari, Inc.
profile: Serial internet entrepreneur who founded Unoh (Movie Life, Photozou, Machitsuku!), sold it to Zynga in 2010, then founded Mercari in Feb 2013. Mercari became Japan's first unicorn and its dominant flea-market app, listed in 2018 (making him a billionaire), and expanded into Merpay, crypto (Mercoin) and the Kashima Antlers football club. He remains CEO.
interesting_fact: As a Waseda University student he interned at a then little-known Rakuten and built its auction site (Rakuten Auction).
deep_cut_fact: In July 2021 he set up the YAMADA Shintaro D&I Foundation with ~3 billion yen of his own money; its flagship is a no-repayment scholarship for girls choosing STEM tracks in high school, now in its 6th cohort (2026). Before Mercari he spent about six months backpacking round the world in cheap hostels.
notes: Foundation donation figure: 30億円 = ~3 billion yen (Business Insider Japan https://www.businessinsider.jp/post-239830). World-trip hostels detail: Japan Times 2016 (https://japantimes.co.jp/news/2016/03/18/business/5-night-hostels-led-japans-first-1-billion-startup, paywalled). Best route: Mercari press form or the D&I foundation.

name: Kanjibhai Virani
current_role: Co-founder, Balaji Wafers Pvt Ltd (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: Kanjibhai (Kanubhai) Virani co-founded Balaji Wafers with brothers Chandubhai and Bhikhubhai; the Rajkot firm grew from wafers sold at a cinema canteen into one of India's largest regional snack makers (chips, namkeen, noodles, confectionery). The family became billionaires after agreeing in Jan 2026 to sell a ~7% minority stake to General Atlantic; the next generation is increasingly running the business.
interesting_fact: The brothers began in 1974 selling wafers from the canteen of Astron Cinema in Rajkot, where they had done odd jobs; wafers were made at home until the first factory opened in 1989. Balaji is said to hold ~90% of Gujarat's chips market.
deep_cut_fact: Their first venture failed: their farmer father Popatbhai sold ancestral farmland to give the brothers Rs 20,000, which they put into farm equipment and lost, before turning to snacks.
notes: Kanjibhai is commonly listed as 'Kanubhai Virani'. Chandubhai Virani is the public face of the company; approach likely via the company. GA deal announced 22 Jan 2026 (https://www.generalatlantic.com/media-article/balaji-wafers-announces-strategic-investment-from-general-atlantic/).
